headline: Apple gains ground as China’s smartphone shipments plunge 15.4% in Q3 2026
summary: Apple's market share in China increased during Q3 2026, despite a 4.3% decline in iPhone shipments amidst a significant overall market drop.
details: According to a new IDC report, Apple's smartphone market share in China grew during Q3 2026. This occurred even as overall smartphone shipments in the region plunged by 15.4% year-over-year.
Despite the market share gain, Apple's own iPhone shipments saw a 4.3% year-over-year decline in the same quarter, highlighting the challenging market conditions for all manufacturers.

topic: industrial next robots automate factory tasks
headline_marked: [[Industrial Next's AI robots retool factories]] in minutes, not weeks
headline: Industrial Next's AI robots retool factories in minutes, not weeks
summary: Industrial Next's AI-driven robotic stations use proprietary foundation models to enable production line retooling in minutes, drastically cutting down on weeks of traditional programming and physical changes.
details: Most factory automation is fixed, requiring weeks or months for reprogramming and retooling when changing production lines. San Francisco-based Industrial Next aims to revolutionize this with its new AI-driven, self-contained robotic stations.

These stations are powered by proprietary foundation models that integrate vision, task context, and motion. This technology allows a production line to be retooled in minutes, eliminating the need for traditional programming and enabling automation of complex, delicate tasks.

Industrial Next announced a partnership with BMW Group Technology Office to evaluate its AI-powered dexterous manipulation for manufacturing applications. This collaboration highlights the potential for significant advancements in industrial automation.

Founded in 2021 by former Tesla engineers Lukas Pankau and Allen Pan, the duo conceived the idea after experiencing firsthand how cutting-edge vehicle and self-driving technology was hindered by decades-old factory equipment.

Traditional industrial robots are programmed for highly specific tasks, leading to costly downtime and product simplification when processes change. The challenge for flexible robots lies in the lack of vast training datasets for complex physical tasks, unlike internet-trained AI models.

Industrial Next addresses this by using an extremely high-fidelity simulation engine that closely mimics real-world physics. This allows their robots to practice and develop an understanding of processes in a virtual environment, enabling high-precision and high-dexterity tasks with minimal physical interaction.
caption:
Factory robots can now switch tasks in minutes, not weeks, thanks to Industrial Next's new AI-driven system.
